parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional mixed-method comparative assessment using questionnaires, interviews, field observations, secondary data, and Rapfish multidimensional scaling
parsed.population_and_sample: Four community-based water-supply systems in two kelurahan of Salatiga City, serving 488 households in total; 168 returned questionnaires (60, 49, 20, and 39 across the four systems).
parsed.exposure: Institutional and management arrangements of community-based water supply, including management legality, organizational structure, SOPs, job descriptions, work schedules, cooperation, reporting, customer service, tariff collection, and government or external support.
parsed.outcome: Water-service sustainability and access-related performance, including coverage, continuity, reliability, customer growth, affordability and willingness to pay, customer satisfaction, and institutional/economic sustainability scores.
parsed.rationale: Section 3 (p. 3) reports primary questionnaire, interview, and field-observation data plus secondary evidence on legal status, organizational rules, SOPs, administration, finance, and consumer participation. Table 1 (p. 3) measures access-relevant outcomes such as continuity, coverage, customer increase, ability to pay, and customer satisfaction, while Sections 4.1–4.2 (pp. 4–5) compare four identifiable CBWS and link weaker institutional management to poorer sustainability.
